text:
olivia: FYI nightly eval flagged a big jump in pset-v52 failure rate after the promptset rename/cleanup PR landed last night. failing cases up ~4.6% vs baseline.

maya: ugh. which tests are spiking?

olivia: mostly date-normalization and 'when is' canonicalization examples. see excerpt from failing cases below.

eval-bot: nightly-evals pset-v52: overall_score -3.2, fail_delta +4.6%, affected_suites: [dates, scheduling, timezones] (run 2318000000)

noah: can you paste a failing example?

olivia: sure — prompt + model output (v2-quantized)

```
PROMPT: "When is the next meeting? It's on 03/04/2025 at 10:00am"
EXPECTED: "March 4, 2025 at 10:00 AM"
MODEL_OUT: "April 3 2025 10:00am"  <-- swapped month/day
```

maya: hmm looks like the normalizer that was introduced to canonicalize dates might be applying US vs ISO heuristics inconsistently after the rename. PR #4821 renamed `normalize_dates` to `normalize_dates_v2` and added a fallback.

lee: I glanced at the PR — the fallback uses a new locale-detect path that tends to prefer DMY for ambiguous numbers. Could explain swapped month/day.

jordan: product impact: some customers rely on canonicalized outputs for calendaring. we should treat this as P1 for pset-v52 canary.

noah: quick triage plan: 1) revert the rename (simple) or 2) patch fallback heuristics, or 3) add a targeted rebaseline for affected prompts. I prefer revert+hotfix to avoid rebaseline noise.

maya: +1 revert, but we should run the revert against quantized variants and the floating-point builds. the quantized runtime in canary gave slightly different tokenization behavior that made the normalized tokens ambiguous.

olivia: started a short run against the canary models with revert applied: run id 2318001200. patch branch: hotfix/normalize-revert-4821.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary cluster (5 nodes) -> branch hotfix/normalize-revert-4821. build 2025.03.21+hotfix-4821.

eval-bot: quick-diff (canary vs nightly): dates_suite fail_delta -3.9% after revert branch applied (preliminary). full report in ~25m.

lee: if revert fixes >90% of the spike we should avoid rebaseline. rebaseline would hide real regressions.

jordan: agree — do revert, run regressions, then we can reintroduce the v2 with a controlled rollout and extra tests for ambiguous dates.

maya: one more note: pset-v52 change also removed an example that highlighted ambiguous DD/MM vs MM/DD. if revert doesn't fully fix, we should add explicit test cases to pset that assert locale disambiguation.

olivia: noted. I'll open a follow-up PR to add 6 edge-case prompts to pset-v52 and pin the expected canonicalization. PR will link to this thread.

noah: thanks. keep the thread updated with the final eval numbers. if we see any other semantic drift (timezones, relative dates) we may need immediate rollback to prior promptset version in prod routing.

olivia: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
